existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: No local `Flag` change appears to make an R4-valid instance invalid in R6. The top concerns are optional `status`, widened `subject` targets, and R6-only `supportingInfo`; the main uncertainty is rationale and terminology context not present in local change notes.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: R6 widens the model rather than narrowing it. Forward migration from R4 to R6 is mostly permissive, but R6-to-R4 conversion must handle missing required R4 `status`, reference targets that R4 did not permit, and the new `supportingInfo` element. Generated classes, validators, and business rules should be retested for absent status and widened reference unions.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural changes because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present and directly compared. Confidence is lower for design rationale and terminology nuance because official diffs, ballot notes, full narrative pages, and terminology expansions were not available locally.

topFindings.title: Flag.status changed from mandatory to optional
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen and R6-to-R4 loss: R6 models must allow a previously mandatory modifier code to be absent, and an R6 Flag with no status cannot be represented as base R4 without inventing active, inactive, or entered-in-error semantics or carrying the unknown state outside the base element.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Flag.subject can now reference RelatedPerson or PractitionerRole
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: an R6 subject reference to RelatedPerson or PractitionerRole is outside the base R4 target list, and substituting Patient, Practitioner, or Organization may change the meaning of what the flag is about. There is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 instance break.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds Flag.supportingInfo as a core element
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss, mostly mitigable: a raw R6 Flag.supportingInfo element is unknown to base R4, but the R4 flag-detail extension provides an explicit representation for the same kind of supporting reference. There is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Flag.author can now reference RelatedPerson
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss with low practical risk: an R6 RelatedPerson author is not a base R4 author target, but the optional non-modifier element can be dropped or transformed when necessary, and no R4-valid author reference becomes invalid in R6.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
